hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: template-svc-1 was restarted by a failed liveness probe at 16:10:28 (#1092), leaving capacity at 3/4. Remaining template-svc capacity was then overwhelmed: admission control reported 590 in-flight requests, 3.2x normal (#1187), and later 827 in-flight at 4.1x baseline with load shedding (#1234), plus queue-full load shedding (#1212). Amplification: notification-svc retries TemplateClient.render immediately with backoff disabled (#1137, #1164, #1205), so every failing request multiplies load on the already-saturated template-svc. Requests then exhaust retries and api-gateway returns 503 after 6-28s (#1186, #1300, #1356, #1474). The fault has not recovered because the retry storm keeps template-svc saturated. The status-poller legacy-inventory timeouts (#299, #353, etc.) are a red herring: that endpoint is deprecated and is not on the notify path. Report-cron job-count churn and notif-db flush lines are noise. The exact cause of the liveness failure is not visible in the logs, so the origin of the trigger is partly unconfirmed.

Alternative reading: template-svc-1 may have run out of resources (its liveness probe failed and it was restarted), and the remaining instances hit their in-flight limit. The logs show GC pauses at normal heap (about 30-43%), so memory exhaustion is not supported by the evidence; the probe failure cause is not logged.

verdict.recommendedAction: Re-enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget on notification-svc's TemplateClient (currently retrying immediately with backoff disabled) to stop the retry storm. Scale template-svc back to full capacity (4/4 or more) and check the template-svc-1 liveness failure cause. Consider temporary load shedding or rate limiting at the gateway for POST /v1/notify until template-svc in-flight drops to baseline. Separately, fix the deprecated legacy-inventory healthcheck in status-poller, which is unrelated noise.
